blocks.text: A2-12 · Numbers with names
Lesson overview

In A1 you have learned the numbers In front of a name, however, the Arabic number follows its own rules, among the most famous of grammar: from three to ten takes the form \"opposed" to the genus of name ( ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ كُتُبٍ⁩ but ⁧ثَلَاثُ سَيَّارَاتٍ⁩ ), and the counted name changes number and case depending on the digit (plural genitive after 3–10, singular accusative after 11–99, singular genitive after 100 and 1000). In this unit learn the complete system up to millions, years, percentages, fractions, prices in Arab currencies and order them over ten. The rules are many: the objective of A2 is use them well with the most frequent names (days, years, hours, people, euros) and recognize the rest. Two weeks.

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-12), scripts for speech synthesis, receipts and flyers with prices, session with the tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
2. Numbers to be allocated 3 a 10 with the name (polarity + plural genitive);
3. use numbers from 11 a 99 with the singular accusative, and ⁧كَمْ⁩ + singular accusative;
4. say and read hundreds, thousands, millions and years;
5. slight percentages, fractions and prices in the main Arab currencies;
6. recognizing the ordinals beyond the ten ( ⁧الحَادِي عَشَرَ⁩ , ⁧القَرْنُ الحَادِي وَالعِشْرُونَ⁩ );
7. buy and ask for prices, give personal data and dates, understand figures in a news.
Two-week plan.

blocks.text: 1. Dialogue 1 · One dinner for ten
Saturday morning. Salmā takes Luca to an Egyptian grocery store in Via Padova, Milan.

rows: ⁧البَائِع: أَهْلًا يَا أُسْتَاذَة سَلْمَى! كَيْفَ حَالُكِ؟⁩
al-bāʾiʿ: ahlan yā ustāḏa Salmā! kayfa ḥāluki?
The storekeeper: Welcome, ma'am Salmā! How are you?
⁧سَلْمَى: بِخَيْرٍ، الحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ. هٰذَا زَمِيلِي لُوكَا. عِنْدِي عَشَاءٌ لِعَشَرَةِ أَشْخَاصٍ يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ، وَأَحْتَاجُ إِلَى أَشْيَاءَ كَثِيرَةٍ.⁩
Salmā: bi-ḫayr, al-ḥamdu li-llāh. hāḏā zamīlī Lūkā. ʿindī ʿašāʾun li-ʿašarati ašḫāṣin yawma s-sabt, wa-aḥtāǧu ilā ašyāʾa kaṯīra.
Salmā: Well, thank God. This is my colleague Luca. I have a dinner on Saturday for ten people and I need a lot of things.
The storekeeper: Please, I'm at your disposal.
⁧سَلْمَى: أُرِيدُ أَرْبَعَةَ أَكْيَاسِ أَرُزٍّ، وَثَلَاثَ زُجَاجَاتِ زَيْتٍ، وَخَمْسَ عُلَبِ شَايٍ.⁩
Salmā: urīdu arbaʿata akyāsi aruzz, wa-ṯalāṯa zuǧāǧāti zayt, wa-ḫamsa ʿulabi šāy.
Salmā: I would like four bags of rice, three bottles of oil and five boxes of tea.
al-bāʾiʿ: wa-l-ḫubz? ʿindanā ḫubzun miṣriyyuni l-yawm.
The storekeeper: What about the bread? Today we have Egyptian bread.
⁧سَلْمَى: مُمْتَاز! اِثْنَيْ عَشَرَ رَغِيفًا، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.⁩
Salmā: mumtāz! iṯnay ʿašara raġīfan, min faḍlik.
⁧لُوكَا: وَأَنَا أُرِيدُ عُلْبَتَيْ قَهْوَةٍ. بِكَمِ العُلْبَةُ؟⁩
Lūkā: wa-ana urīdu ʿulbatay qahwa. bi- kami l-ʿulba?
And I'd like two packs of coffee. How much is one?
⁧البَائِع: العُلْبَةُ بِأَرْبَعَةِ يُورُو، وَالعُلْبَتَانِ بِسَبْعَةٍ فَقَطْ.⁩
al-bāʾiʿ: al-ʿulbatu bi-arbaʿati yūrū, wa- l-ʿulbatāni bi-sabʿatin faqaṭ.
The storekeeper: One costs four euros, two only seven.
… ⁧أَرُزٌّ، زَيْتٌ، شَايٌ، خُبْزٌ، قَهْوَةٌ⁩ : ⁧البَائِع⁩ ⁧المَجْمُوعُ سِتَّةٌ وَأَرْبَعُونَ يُورُو وَنِصْفٌ.⁩
al-bāʾiʿ: aruzz, zayt, šāy, ḫubz, qahwa… al-maǧmūʿu sittatun wa- arbaʿūna yūrū wa-niṣf.
The shopkeeper: Rice, oil, tea, bread, coffee... The total is forty-six euro and a half.
al-bāʾiʿ: wa-hāḏā l-bāqī: ṯalāṯatu yūrū wa-niṣf.
The shopkeeper: And here's the rest: three and a half euros.
⁧لُوكَا: مُنْذُ مَتَى تَعْمَلُ فِي هٰذَا المَحَلِّ؟⁩
Lūkā: munḏu matā taʿmalu fī hāḏā l- maḥall?
Luca: How long have you been working in this store?
⁧البَائِع: مُنْذُ اثْنَتَيْنِ وَعِشْرِينَ سَنَةً! جِئْتُ إِلَى مِيلَانُو عَامَ أَلْفَيْنِ وَأَرْبَعَةٍ.⁩
al-bāʾiʿ: munḏu ṯnatayni wa-ʿišrīna sana! ǧiʾtu ilā Mīlānū ʿāma alfayni wa- arbaʿa.
The storekeeper: For 22 years! I arrived in Milan in 2004.
⁧سَلْمَى: هُوَ يَعْرِفُ كُلَّ المِصْرِيِّينَ فِي الحَيِّ!⁩
Salmā: huwa yaʿrifu kulla l-miṣriyyīna fī l-ḥayy!
Salmā: He knows all the Egyptians in the neighborhood!
al-bāʾiʿ: lā, laysa kullahum… ḫamsamiʾatin faqaṭ!
The storekeeper: No, not all... only 500!

What to notice. ⁧أَرْبَعَةَ أَكْيَاسٍ⁩ , ⁧ثَلَاثَ زُجَاجَاتٍ⁩ , ⁧خَمْسَ عُلَبٍ⁩ , ⁧عَشَرَةِ أَشْخَاصٍ⁩ : 3 a 10 the name goes to the plural genitive and the number has the shape with ⁧ة⁩ if the singular name is male ( ⁧كِيس⁩ , ⁧شَخْص⁩ ), without ⁧ة⁩ if you are female ( ⁧زُجَاجَة⁩ , ⁧عُلْبَة⁩ ). 2. One and two.

rows: two books · two (and no more) machines

blocks.text: “One” uses the singular noun; “two” uses the dual. Not said. ⁧وَاحِد كِتَاب⁩ . ⁧وَاحِد⁩ and ⁧اِثْنَان⁩ are added after the name, as adjectives that agree, only to insist on the number: ⁧غُرْفَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ فَقَطْ⁩ One room is one. One of them, one of them. ⁧أَحَدُ⁩ ( m.) / ⁧إِحْدَى⁩ (f.) + plural determined, in iḍāfa: ⁧أَحَدُ الطُّلَّابِ⁩ • one of the students • ⁧إِحْدَى المُوَظَّفَاتِ⁩ (a) one of the employees (a) ⁧أَحَدُهُمْ⁩ One of them is. In the news it is very frequent: ⁧أَحَدُ المَسْؤُولِينَ⁩ • a person in charge.
3. Three to ten: polarity
Three rules:
1. The number comes first and the name follows it in iḍāfa, to the undetermined plural genitive: ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ كُتُبٍ⁩ .

2. Polarity. If the singular name is masculine, the number has the ⁧ة⁩ ; If it's feminine, it doesn't. Count on singular, not plural: ⁧رَجُل⁩ ( m.) → ⁧خَمْسَةُ رِجَالٍ⁩ ; ⁧اِمْرَأَة⁩ ( f.) → ⁧خَمْسُ نِسَاءٍ⁩ ; ⁧لَيْلَة⁩ ( f.) → ⁧سَبْعُ لَيَالٍ⁩ , although ⁧لَيَالٍ⁩ has no ⁧ة⁩ .

3. The number declines as a name: ⁧رَأَيْتُ ثَلَاثَةَ رِجَالٍ⁩ I saw three men. ⁧فِي خَمْسَةِ أَيَّامٍ⁩ In five days. The name stays with the genitive. Attention to shapes. ⁧عَشَرَةُ⁩ ( ʿašaratu) with male children, ⁧عَشْرُ⁩ ( ʿašru) with the female: also the vowel changes. ⁧ثَمَانِيَةُ⁩ with males, ⁧ثَمَانِي⁩ ( ṯamānī) with women. The diptotes remain such: ⁧سَبْعَةُ أَسَابِيعَ⁩ , ⁧تِسْعُ دَقَائِقَ⁩ ( A2-08). With the article the number usually follows the name as adjective: ⁧الأَيَّامُ الثَّلَاثَةُ⁩ The three-day period shall be: ⁧السَّنَوَاتُ الخَمْسُ⁩ The five years are the same. It is also found ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ الأَيَّامِ⁩ , less frequent. A trick to remember. With the male names the number appears feminine, and vice versa. Think about ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ أَيَّامٍ⁩ and ⁧ثَلَاثُ سَاعَاتٍ⁩ like models and repeat them until they sound natural.
4. From 11 a 19
19 ⁧تِسْعَ عَشْرَةَ صَفْحَةًتِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ كِتَابًا⁩
The rules:
1. The name goes to the singular indeterminate accusative: ⁧خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا⁩ (Lett. 15 as per day).
2. 11 and 12 they agree in both parts: ⁧أَحَدَ عَشَرَ⁩ ( m.) / ⁧إِحْدَى عَشْرَةَ⁩ ( f.).
3. From 13 a 19 the unit follows polarity (as 3–9), the second part shall agree: ⁧ثَلَاثَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا⁩ , ⁧ثَلَاثَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً⁩ .

4. The two sides end up in -a and don't decline, except 12: ⁧اِثْنَا عَشَرَ⁩ (name) / ⁧اِثْنَيْ عَشَرَ⁩ (genitive and The Court ruled: ⁧عَشَرَ⁩ and ⁧عَشْرَةَ⁩ . In numbers 11–19, with the male they say ʿašara (without ⁧ة⁩ ), with women ʿašrata (with ⁧ة⁩ and without vowel on the š): the opposite of what happens with the 10 alone.
5. From 20 a 99, e ⁧كَمْ⁩
The tens have only one form for the two genera and decline as a healthy plural: -ūna the name, -īna to the genitive and the accusative.
The composite numbers are called units + ⁧وَ⁩ + 10 , as in German (- 1 and 20 ,):
99 ⁧تِسْعٌ وَتِسْعُونَ دَقِيقَةًتِسْعَةٌ وَتِسْعُونَ يُورُو⁩

The name goes to the singular accusative, as after 11–19. The unit follows the rules of 1–2 (agreement) and 3–9 (polarity); both sides decline: ⁧فِي خَمْسَةٍ وَعِشْرِينَ يَوْمًا⁩ In twenty-five days. Age. ⁧عُمْرِي خَمْسٌ وَثَلَاثُونَ سَنَةً⁩ I'm 35 years old. ⁧سَنَة⁩ is female: ⁧خَمْسٌ⁩ without ⁧ة⁩ ). Many say simply ⁧عُمْرِي خَمْسَةٌ وَثَلَاثُونَ⁩ , without a name. ⁧كَمْ⁩ + singular accusative. How many? ⁧كَمْ⁩ followed by the name to the singular accusative, as after 11–99: ⁧كَمْ طَالِبًا فِي الصَّفِّ؟⁩ How many students are there in the classroom? ⁧كَمْ سَنَةً عِشْتَ فِي القَاهِرَةِ؟⁩ How many years have you lived in Cairo? With the price: ⁧بِكَمْ⁩ … ⁧؟⁩ - How much...?

blocks.text: — ⁧يُورُو⁩ ⁧يُورُو⁩ ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ يُورُو⁩

In Egypt the lira ( ⁧جُنَيْه⁩ ) is divided into one hundred plates ( ⁧قِرْش⁩ ). Currency are names like the others and follow the rules of the number: ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ دَنَانِيرَ⁩ ( ⁧دِينَار⁩ m.), ⁧ثَلَاثُ لِيرَاتٍ⁩ ( ⁧لِيرَة⁩ f.). ⁧يُورُو⁩ It never changes. To ask: ⁧بِكَمْ هٰذَا؟⁩ How much does it cost? ⁧كَمِ السِّعْرُ؟⁩ What is the price? ⁧كَمِ المَجْمُوعُ؟⁩ How much is it in everything? Half and quarter. ⁧خَمْسَةُ يُورُو وَنِصْفٌ⁩ 5 and a half euros; ⁧نِصْفُ كِيلُو⁩ • half a kilo • ⁧رُبْعُ سَاعَةٍ⁩ It's a quarter of an hour.
7. Dialogue 2 · Registration for the course
Tuesday night. Luca calls the language center in Cairo where he works Ṭāriq.

The secretary: Language Center, good evening.
⁧لُوكَا: مَسَاءَ النُّورِ. أَنَا لُوكَا، صَدِيقُ طَارِق. أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُسَجِّلَ فِي الدَّوْرَةِ المُكَثَّفَةِ.⁩

blocks.text: What to notice. The dates are read with the order: ⁧١٣ يُولْيُو⁩ = ⁧الثَّالِثَ عَشَرَ مِنْ يُولْيُو⁩ (Section 10); In conversation many use the cardinal. ⁧عَامَ أَلْفٍ وَتِسْعِمِئَةٍ وَوَاحِدٍ وَتِسْعِينَ⁩ : years (section 8). ⁧ثَمَانِيَةُ أَيَّامٍ⁩ ( ⁧يَوْم⁩ m.) but ⁧اِثْنَتَانِ وَثَلَاثُونَ سَاعَةً⁩ ( ⁧سَاعَة⁩ f.). ⁧كَمْ طَالِبًا: كَمْ⁩ + singular accusative. ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ إِيطَالِيِّينَ⁩ : the healthy plural after 3–10. ⁧أَرْبَعُمِئَةِ يُورُو⁩ , ⁧ثَلَاثُمِئَةٍ وَعِشْرُونَ⁩ , ⁧مِئَتَانِ وَثَمَانِيَةٌ وَثَمَانُونَ⁩ : the hundreds (section 7). ⁧بِنِسْبَةِ عَشَرَةٍ فِي المِئَةِ⁩ 10 per cent (section) 9). ⁧عَلَى الأَكْثَرِ⁩ The maximum value of the product shall be: ⁧نَاقِصَ⁩ • minus • is used in calculations. The 23 July in Egypt is national holiday: recalls the revolution of 1952. Course prices are invented.
8. One hundred, one thousand, millions
2000 ⁧أَلْفَا دُولَارٍأَلْفَيْنِ⁩ / ⁧أَلْفَانِ⁩ ( iḍāfa: without ⁧ن⁩ )

After a hundred, a thousand, a million, the name goes to the singular genitive: ⁧مِئَةُ يُورُو⁩ , ⁧أَلْفُ سَنَةٍ⁩ , ⁧مِلْيُونُ شَخْصٍ⁩ . ⁧أَلْف⁩ is male, ⁧مِئَة⁩ is feminine, and they also follow polarity: ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ آلَافٍ⁩ ( ⁧ة⁩ , why ⁧أَلْف⁩ is male), but ⁧ثَلَاثُمِئَةٍ⁩ (without ⁧ة⁩ , why ⁧مِئَة⁩ is female). Hundreds from 300 a 900 they write in one word. Long numbers are said to be from the largest to the smallest, but the last block is left + ⁧وَ⁩ + ten (s): 1250 = ⁧أَلْفٌ وَمِئَتَانِ وَخَمْسُونَ⁩ ; 2026 = ⁧أَلْفَانِ وَسِتَّةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ⁩ . The name follows the last element: 1250 ⁧طَالِبًا⁩ (after 50: singular accusative); 1300 ⁧طَالِبٍ⁩ (after 300: singular genitive); 103 = ⁧مِئَةٌ وَثَلَاثَةُ طُلَّابٍ⁩ (after 3: plural genitive). In practice. In the texts the big numbers are almost always written in figures; who reads aloud, especially in the speech, often simplifies the endings (use -īna for the tens in any case, the polarity is wrong in the long numbers). You are asked to understand the big numbers and to say the name rule well after the number.
9. Years and dates
Years are introduced with ⁧عَامَ⁩ or ⁧سَنَةَ⁩ the accused person (-) followed by the number to the genitive. With ⁧عَام⁩ (male) units 3 a 9 they take the ⁧ة⁩ :

Abbreviations. After the year there is often a letter: ⁧م⁩ stands for ⁧مِيلَادِيّ⁩ "of the Christian era" ⁧هـ⁩ stands for ⁧هِجْرِيّ⁩ Egira () (L0-10). Example: ⁧٢٠٢٦م⁩ . Decades: ⁧فِي التِّسْعِينِيَّاتِ⁩ In the 1990s, ⁧فِي السَّبْعِينِيَّاتِ⁩ In the 1970s. Centuries: ⁧القَرْنُ العِشْرُونَ⁩ The 20th century (section) 10). Dates (A1-17): ⁧١٤ أُكْتُوبَر ٢٠٢٦⁩ read ⁧الرَّابِعَ عَشَرَ مِنْ أُكْتُوبَرَ عَامَ أَلْفَيْنِ وَسِتَّةٍ وَعِشْرِينَ⁩ ; in the talk many say ⁧أَرْبَعَةَ عَشَرَ أُكْتُوبَر⁩ . For the date of birth / in the day of use ⁧مَوْلُودٌ⁩ / ⁧مَوْلُودَةٌ فِي⁩ …: ⁧مَوْلُودٌ فِي ٣ مَارِس ١٩٩١⁩ d.o.b 3 March 1991».
10. Percentages, fractions, order numbers

Percentages. The sign is ⁧٪⁩ and we read ⁧بِالمِئَةِ⁩ (or ⁧فِي المِئَةِ⁩ ). For example ⁧٣٠٪⁩ read ⁧ثَلَاثُونَ بِالمِئَةِ⁩ . Of the 30 %/day after a verb or name: ⁧بِنِسْبَةِ ثَلَاثِينَ بِالمِئَةِ⁩ . In the news: ⁧اِرْتَفَعَتِ الأَسْعَارُ بِنِسْبَةِ خَمْسَةٍ فِي المِئَةِ⁩ Prices increased by 5 %». Decimals write with the Arabic comma ⁧٫⁩ ( ⁧٥٫٢⁩ ) and read with ⁧فَاصِلَة⁩ : ⁧اِثْنَانِ فَاصِلَة خَمْسَة⁩ (to be recognized). Fractions. ⁧نِصْف⁩ "Middle" ⁧ثُلُث⁩ A third of the following is added: ⁧رُبْع⁩ A quarter of the total value of all the materials used does not exceed 50% of the ex-works price of the product ⁧خُمْس⁩ A fifth of this Regulation shall apply from 1 January 2017. ⁧عُشْر⁩ It's a tenth of a decade. Dual and plural: ⁧ثُلُثَانِ⁩ "Two thirds', ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ أَرْبَاعٍ⁩ “three quarters”. They are built in iḍāfa: ⁧نِصْفُ السُّكَّانِ⁩ Half of the inhabitants of the island, ⁧رُبْعُ سَاعَةٍ⁩ It's a quarter of an hour. Order them over ten (recognize). From 11 a 19 the unit + order is used ⁧عَشَرَ⁩ / ⁧عَشْرَةَ⁩ , all in -a; from 20 then the ten is the same as the cardinal, with the article.

Frequent examples: ⁧القَرْنُ الحَادِي وَالعِشْرُونَ⁩ The 21st Century... ⁧الطَّابِقُ الثَّانِي عَشَرَ⁩ The 12th floor is: ⁧السَّاعَةُ الحَادِيَةَ عَشْرَةَ⁩ 11 (A1-17), ⁧الذِّكْرَى الخَمْسُونَ⁩ It's the 50th anniversary of that. ⁧الحَادِي⁩ , variant of ⁧وَاحِد⁩ , is used only in compounds: by itself is ⁧الأَوَّل⁩ .
11. Pronunciation

Long numbers. Practice reading numbers from unit to ten: 47 = sabʿatun wa-arbaʿūn, 7:40. It's the most frequent mistake of Italians: say ""arbaʿūn wa-sabʿa». ṯalāṯa, ṯamāniya. Three and eight begin with ⁧ث⁩ (as in English think), not with t o s. ʿašara / ʿašr / ʿašrata. Three different forms of the ten: ⁧عَشَرَةُ أَيَّامٍ⁩ ( ʿašaratu), ⁧عَشْرُ سَنَوَاتٍ⁩ ( ʿašru), ⁧خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً⁩ ( ʿašrata). miʾa. ⁧مِائَة⁩ It's written with an alif that doesn't say: miʾa, nevermāʾa». Sit down. ⁧سِتَّة⁩ has a double t: sit-ta.

Notes of use. The tens must be learned with the two forms: in a vocalized text you will see both ⁧عِشْرُونَ⁩ is ⁧عِشْرِينَ⁩ . ⁧رُسُوم⁩ is the plural of ⁧رَسْم⁩ • tax, but ⁧رَسْم⁩ to the singular means also 'design': the university fees are ⁧الرُّسُومُ الدِّرَاسِيَّةُ⁩ . ⁧يُسَجِّلُ⁩ has many uses: ⁧سَجَّلَ اسْمَهُ⁩ "His name is registered under the name of the person, ⁧سَجَّلْتُ فِي الدَّوْرَةِ⁩ I enrolled in the course. ⁧سَجَّلَ هَدَفًا⁩ He scored a goal (sport). ⁧اِرْتَفَعَ⁩ and ⁧اِنْخَفَضَ⁩ are the verbs of the news with figures: ⁧اِرْتَفَعَ عَدَدُ الزُّوَّارِ⁩ The number of visitors has increased. ⁧نَسَمَة⁩ is used only to count the population: ⁧مِصْرُ⁩ : ⁧أَكْثَرُ مِنْ ١٠٠ مِلْيُونِ نَسَمَةٍ⁩ . It recalls the price pluralities: ⁧خَمْسَةُ دَنَانِيرَ⁩ , ⁧عَشَرَةُ دَرَاهِمَ⁩ (diptotics).

Listen to the B script and write each number in digits and the name that follows it. Then you rewrite everything in letters, vocalized.
Exercise 16 · A short text with data (week 68)

Write a text of about 80 words, vocalized, that present with numbers a place you know well: your office, your palace, your country or your city. You can invent the data. Required elements: at least one number from 3 a 10 with a male name and one with a female name, a number from 11 a 19, a number from 21 a 99, a number with ⁧مِئَة⁩ or ⁧أَلْف⁩ , one year, a percentage or a fraction, a question with ⁧كَمْ⁩ .

18. Oral production
1. At the market. Roleplay with the tutor: buy five different products (quantity between 2 and 15), ask for prices, contracts for a discount, pay and check the rest.

2. Personal data and dates (session). The tutor plays the part of an employee filling out a form: date and place of birth, years of service, number of family members, dates of a trip. Answer with full sentences; Then you switch roles.
3. Numbers in news. Read the reading aloud 2 and the news of the C script, then summarize it in English quoting the figures.
